doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: Be yourself: the takeaway from interviews
summary: Interviews with Miles, Rollins, Blakey and others taught him to be himself and stop comparing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: sound like somebody else you’re doomed to be second best, they’re already doing it. So at some point I really settled into owning my playing and not worrying about whether it was I don’t know, authentically part of the tradition or — I stopped comparing my performance and the time I put in and my practicing — I stopped comparing it with my hopes and dreams from being a 13-year-old kid or whatever, and just accepted it, and that really came from conversations with all — I mean Miles Davis, Sonny Rollins, Art Blakey, anybody you talk to will tell you that. And that’s the takeaway, you know like I said to I think it was Herbie Hancock or whatever, like what was the influence of being with Miles, and everybody said the same thing, be yourself. That was the whole takeaway. Not this note, that chord, this approach, just be yourself.

Did you have a particular question, you sort of just answered it but it was specific to Miles, but I have a question that I usually ask about improvising, what are you thinking about when you’re improvising. And I almost always get the same basic answer. I’m not going to say what it is, I mean I could, but I wonder if you’ve had questions like that, that you usually find the same answer?
